title: The Mist Goblin Legend Murder Case
subtitle_source: case_closed_dataset/subs_resolved/0052.txt (775 dialogue lines, full transcript read, 60-minute special episode)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object), sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. Unusually, the victim of the present-day murder (Tenei) is himself the perpetrator of the backstory murder (Chunen, 2 years earlier) -- both his own has_motive_against edge (against Chunen) and the true culprit's has_motive_against edge (against Tenei) are recorded. Kannen's oddly quick, oddly certain discovery of both bodies is flagged as a genuine red-herring suspicion the transcript raises but never resolves into a motive, so no fabricated has_motive_against edge was added for him. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The recovered drainboard has a deliberately shortened, warped cut and tape residue, with cherry-blossom petals from the waterfall trapped underneath -- proving it was flipped and taped to divert the adjacent waterfall through the window, flooding the room to float a body up to the beam without leaving any hoist marks.

Shunen claimed to have heard Ran's scream at the Tengu mask while reading in his own room until past 3:00am, but the killer's method requires being sealed inside the meditation room next to a roaring waterfall for hours that night -- a setting that would drown out any distant scream, contradicting his claim to have heard it.

Fingerprints were found on the tape still stuck to the one wood fragment from the sliding panel that the killer failed to recover, having been thrown clear into the woods when the flooded wall gave way.
